title: SSpMV: A Sparsity-aware SpMV Framework Empowered by Multimodal Machine Learning
problem: Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication performance varies significantly across matrices and architectures; existing SpMV libraries use fixed algorithms that do not adapt to matrix sparsity patterns and hardware characteristics.
motivation: SpMV is fundamental to scientific computing and AI; adaptive algorithm selection based on sparse pattern recognition can dramatically improve performance across diverse matrices.
method: SSpMV combines expert-designed matrix measurements with a machine learning model called MM-Adapter that analyzes multiple characteristics of a sparse matrix (its sparsity patterns, density, and structure) to predict the fastest-running algorithm. Rather than using the same algorithm for every matrix, it learns which matrix features correspond to which algorithms, then selects the best algorithm and settings for each specific matrix.
key_novelty: It uses machine learning that examines multiple types of information about matrices—expert measurements and patterns learned from data—to automatically pick the best algorithm instead of using one fixed algorithm for all cases.
contributions: MM-Adapter multimodal network for SpMV algorithm prediction
Integration of expert-designed features with learned modalities
Consistent performance improvements over state-of-the-art sparse libraries across multi-core platforms
limitations: Performance improvements not quantified in abstract; limited to multi-core CPUs, GPU acceleration not discussed.
primary_theme: multimodal machine learning for adaptive SpMV selection
